format.summary: Every spoken or displayed sentence of the conversation. The model listens, rules decide, these templates speak: code fills every {var} and never writes wording of its own.
format.message: messages.<key> = {group, channels, phone|web|all, closed?, short?, expect?, vars, notes?}.
format.channels: Where the key is used: phone, web or both. phone/web/all are lists of variants; a channel uses its own list, else all. all is always phone-safe.
format.spanish: Phone conversations are English only. The es bank carries phone variants only for phone-only keys; only language.offer_web and line.* are ever spoken in Spanish on the phone.
format.variant: A string, or {say, ask}. A string in a key with expect is the ask; otherwise it is said. {say, ask} gives both parts (the opening, close.anything_else, re-ask lines).
format.pick: Variant = hash(call_id, key, turn) % n, deterministic.
format.question_var: {question} is the pending question's ask, rendered by code (for a {say, ask} key only the ask part): main form after the 1st silence and after an interruption, closed form after the 2nd silence and after an unclear answer, short form after any other line (ssn.block, card_number.block, info lines). The reply then uses that question's expect and listen.
format.closed: closed = the same question as a yes/no or a choice of at most three single keys, with the keypad option on the phone ('press one for yes, two for no'; 'press one, two, or three') and tap choices on the web. Used in closed mode (model late or failing), after an unclear answer, and after the 2nd silence. closed.expect overrides expect when present. Money questions are answered by voice; their closed form is a spoken band choice (ask.rent, expedited.intro_cash, ask.income_band, flip.other_cash_band) or a yes/no that leads to one (ask.income -> ask.income_band; ask.other_cash -> flip.other_cash_band). The phone never asks for a typed number: the gateway sends one key per event and never collects digits (docs/BRAIN_API.md, TurnRequest keypad note).
format.short: short = a brief re-ask used after another line in the same reply, so phone replies stay inside the word budget.
format.expect: {expect, listen, slots, keypad, choices, band_edges?, yes?, no?}. expect and listen use the Brain API enums. slots = what the question asks for. keypad: null, 'yes_no' (1 = yes, 2 = no), or {key: entry} with single keys '1' to '3' (at most three). No multi-key entry: no amounts or ages typed on the keypad, no '#'. choices = web quick replies, each {label, entry}. Entry = {set: {slot: value}} | {band: token} | {intent: name} | {answer: yes|no} | {action: name} | {note}. yes/no say what a yes or no means when the slot is not a plain boolean. band_edges = {a, b}: fixed edges for a band choice on a key that has no a and b vars.
format.budgets: Phone say + ask: opening 40, question 25, result 45 words (contract word = whitespace token with a letter or digit). Result class = result.*, expedited.yes|maybe, first_month.*, card.*, close.anything_else, close.silence, or any line with a phone number. Build a reply key by key; when the next key would push it over its budget, end the reply there (ask null) and give the rest on the next turn, as in the contract's Jamal example. flip.intro precedes the first flip question of a call when the whole reply (say + ask) stays within 25 words, read-back included; otherwise it is dropped. Maria's flip reply is readback.rent + flip.intro + flip.rent_paid_by_others (24 of 25 words with her values). readback.cash is never spoken after the cash answer (see confirm_policy). check_content.py lists the compositions that are known to fit.
format.entry_values: set values are raw answers that code normalizes like any other answer (money '0' -> '0.00'; booleans 'true'/'false'). For rent_paid_by_others_to_landlord the value 'rent_share' means the whole rent share. Band tokens: below_a (under a), between (a up to b), above_b (more than b) for ask.income_band and flip.other_cash_band (a and b are vars) and for the closed band choices of ask.rent, expedited.intro_cash and ask.age_parent (a and b are the key's band_edges); below_x, above_x for flip.earned_split. A band answer is a range, not a value, handled like ask.income_band: code keeps the range, uses its conservative end (the end that gives the lower estimate), lets the question plan narrow it where it can, and leaves a yellow line for a range still open at the result; the expedited outlook is computed over the whole range (yes, maybe or no).
format.renamed: Older draft names that are not used: card.phone (now card.phone_screen | card.phone_code); human.handoff (now human.request; no hand-off field exists); line.timeout_reask and line.error_goodbye (now the seven line.* keys of GET /v1/lines); expect.kind (now expect.expect, the Brain API enum, plus expect.listen).
format.never: No rejection wording, no promise of texts, callbacks, live hand-off, reminders or 'sent to the coordinator', no 'any language', no eligibility decision, no claim of fewer errors. data/content/guards.json output.forbidden is the list; check_content.py enforces it on every variant.
format.confirm: Explicit confirm (confirm.money) only for the slots in confirm_policy.confirm_slots, and only when the parser and the model disagree, a teen/ty word is involved, confidence is under 0.75, or the value is out of range. One explicit confirm per slot; still unclear -> conservative value + yellow line. Every other slot is accepted as heard. cash_on_hand gets neither a confirm nor a read-back.

var_types.money: an amount; code verbalizes it on the phone and formats it ($306) on the web
var_types.text: text rendered by code from this bank (a question) or from spoken.period

spoken.money: Whole dollars in words. Under 1,000: 306 -> 'three hundred six dollars', 900 -> 'nine hundred dollars'. 1,000-9,999 with a hundreds digit other than zero: say hundreds, 1100 -> 'eleven hundred dollars', 1975 -> 'nineteen hundred seventy-five dollars', 2500 -> 'twenty-five hundred dollars'. Whole thousands, a zero hundreds digit, and 10,000 or more: say thousands, 2000 -> 'two thousand dollars', 1050 -> 'one thousand fifty dollars', 12197 -> 'twelve thousand one hundred ninety-seven dollars'. Hourly rates keep cents: 18.50 -> 'eighteen dollars fifty'.
